description: Brain says encoding agent runs every stop. Conversation reveals it now runs every 5th stop via daemon gating. Should revise, not duplicate.

required_nodes: Encoding agent runs on every Stop event

exchanges.content: The token savings from the encoding gating are significant. Only firing every 5th stop cuts costs by 80%.
Right — the daemon owns the counter now. On 4 out of 5 stops, stop_agent_prompt returns NONE and the agent bails immediately. On the 5th stop, the daemon inlines the full encoding instructions.
The key insight was having the agent ASK the daemon for its prompt rather than always getting the full instructions. Tiny prompt, one eval call, done.

And the race condition is handled naturally — the command hook hits the daemon in <100ms while the agent needs seconds to parse its prompt and make the eval call. By the time it checks, the counter is already updated.
